in return for, instead of
for, i.e. in place of someone.
for the sake of or as a penalty for something.

Thus Auratus correctly for ἀντεπίξηνον νεί αντεπίξεινον [instead of a chopping-block or instead of a guest], although against the rule of the grammarians, who do not allow anastrophe of the preposition ἀντί [instead of].
After ἄλλος [another]
I choose this word from you in return for those.
And instead of men, arms and ashes come to each man's house.
And instead of funeral laments, a paean — may he bring.
But instead of the ancestral altar, a chopping-block awaits.
But this deed was done against all in return for one.
But you, instead of speech, indicate with barbarian hand.
No one else in my place.
Enrich some other ruin (thus Stanley for στην) in my place.
In return for which you will guard this joyless rock.
to impose a graceless favor unjustly in return for great deeds
This reproach comes in return for reproach.
When a woman dies in my place for a woman, and a man ill-mated falls in place of a man.
Instead of a hostile tongue, let a hostile tongue be accomplished.
And instead of a murderous blow, let him pay a murderous blow.
For someone pouring out everything in return for one blood, the toil is in vain.
May you abound with good things in return for good things.

after which words Weil noticed that a verse had fallen out, whose sense would have been τίνοντας ὧν ἔδρασαν ἀξίαν κακῶν [paying the worthy penalty for the evils they did]. In the margin of M is written γρ. ἀντικατακτανεῖν [variant: to kill in turn].
